g-kokkos.name: Kokkos Cafe Bistro
g-kokkos.teaser: Where the strip's residents hold the meeting, then stay on through lunch over a kokkoccino
g-kokkos.story: The café Diani's long-stayers, NGO staff and hotel managers treat as an office with espresso: the meeting at ten turns into weekday lunch and then into the afternoon. Linger on a weekday; on Sunday it shuts early.
facts: A kokkoccino, the house flavoured cappuccino
Weekday lunch; Mon–Sat 08:00–23:00, Sun 09:00–16:30 (own site, stale: confirm Sunday; seen Aug 2026)

g-bakehouse.name: Diani Bakehouse
g-bakehouse.teaser: Berliners and a German seed loaf to carry next door, if the oven is still on: check first
g-bakehouse.story: Not a place to sit out the afternoon: buy the morning bake and take it to a table at Kokkos. It publishes almost nothing, so check @diani_bakehouse on Instagram before crossing town.
facts: A German seed loaf and a jam-filled Berliner
Early, while the bake is fresh; hours unpublished, liveness unproven (seen Aug 2026)
Cakes to order; otherwise walk in

g-skippers.name: Skippers Coliving
g-skippers.teaser: Two internet lines, triple power backup, desks in cool rooms: the one address in Diani built for work
g-skippers.story: Every other address in this section is a café that tolerates laptops. Skippers was built for the opposite. Opened in 2023 near the airstrip by Duncan and Camilla, two nomads who had spent six years living on a boat, it is a village of air-conditioned container rooms with desks, a coworking room running Starlink and fibre load-balanced together, triple power backup, a wood-fired pizzeria, a gym and a plunge pool. It is not a drop-in. Four-week stays are preferred, short stays fill the gaps, and outside day use is a low-season favour you ask for politely. On Thursdays the residents shut the screens for live music.
g-skippers.why: Book it if work is the trip; if work is an hour, a café will do.
facts: Low season only, and only by asking
Thursday nights for the live music

g-pallet.name: Pallet Cafe, Galu
g-pallet.teaser: The loveliest desk on the coast, on Galu sand, with glare and patchy 4G thrown in
g-pallet.story: The coworking corner sits in a café with no walls, beach beds and hammocks, where you order coffee in the basic sign printed on the menu; the honest work-truth is salt breeze, screen glare and a signal that comes and goes. Beautiful. Close the laptop.
facts: Barista coffee, signed across the counter
Weekday morning; reported 09:00–16:00, confirm on Instagram (seen Aug 2026)
Walk in; WhatsApp for the desk corner

g-asha.name: Asha Boutique Bistro
g-asha.teaser: Outlets, wifi and the ocean in view: laptop at lunch, never on a Friday night
g-asha.story: The one beach-side bistro where a 2022 work survey found real power, workable wifi (30 down) and palm shade that keeps sand off the keys; the figures are four years old, so test the line before a call. On Friday the all-you-can-eat BBQ and live guitar take over, and the laptop goes back in the bag.
facts: Lunch from the Indian Ocean seafood plates
Walk in by day; call +254 115 065 158 to check hours

b-41.name: The 41 Beach Club
b-41.teaser: Where the Forty Thieves crowd went: a sundowner under an ancient baobab, bao on the counter
b-41.story: Take the drink at the bar built round the baobab late on a Saturday, the most sociable afternoon on the strip, or take it to sea on the sundowner dhow. Jazz nights are on the calendar; the founders' story is in the full card.
facts: A sundowner at the baobab bar, or the dhow cruise
Saturday afternoon into sunset; Sun–Thu 11:00–22:00, Fri–Sat to 23:00 (seen Aug 2026)
Walk in on weekdays; reserve weekends on WhatsApp, +254 758 423 283
Sundowner dhow KES 5,000; sunbed KES 1,500 (seen Aug 2026)

b-sails.name: Sails at Almanara
b-sails.teaser: One drink under white canvas on Galu while the sail canopies catch the last light
b-sails.story: Day visitors are formally welcome, so you need not stay for chef Anthony Huth's dinner to have the most graceful sundowner on Galu. Book a sunset table; on full-moon nights dinner moves out onto the sand.
facts: Golden hour; hours unpublished, call ahead
Top band; no prices published, so ask first

b-salty.name: Salty Squid at kite-o'clock
b-salty.teaser: A chilli-mango margarita while the kite instructors land in front of the terrace
b-salty.story: Sit for sunset on the Kenyaways compound, next door to the H2O Extreme kite school, and the show is Galu's sky traffic on final approach. Order the garlic king prawns with it, and come early: this is a sunset room.
facts: Chilli-mango margarita and garlic king prawns
Sunset in kite season (mid-Dec to mid-Mar, Jun to mid-Sep); bar to 21:30, food to 20:30

b-funky.name: Funky Monkey
b-funky.teaser: A smoked Negroni in a roadside courtyard, from a bar team ranked three years running
b-funky.story: No sea view, and none needed: this courtyard was the first bar on the Kenyan coast listed on 50 Best Discovery, and a Spirited Awards Middle East & Africa Top-10 honoree in 2024, 2025 and 2026. Come once the sun has gone and the beach bars wind down.
facts: The smoked Negroni, or the pineapple-basil smash
After dark; Sun–Tue to 23:00, Wed–Sat to midnight (seen Aug 2026)

b-manyatta.name: Manyatta
b-manyatta.teaser: Where Ukunda itself drinks and dances: Kenyan prices, Kenyan playlists, no polish
b-manyatta.story: The counterweight to the beach-bar circuit: a bar, restaurant and disco with no tourist premium, named in the May 2024 press reports on the strip's nightlife revival, when new streetlights brought people back onto the beach road after dark. It has no current channel of its own, the thinnest paper trail of any club here, which is partly why it is still the local one. For a chef at ease in Kenyan bars it is the real thing; guests may be happier on the sand. Full Moon and Tandoori were also listed in 2024, nothing verifiable.
b-manyatta.why: Go with a local driver who knows the door, or not at all.
facts: Unverified in 2026: no website or social channel found

b-shakatak.name: Shakatak
b-shakatak.teaser: Thirty-plus years of coast disco by its own count, and a website that stops in March 2023
b-shakatak.story: Run by German operator Lutz Augenreich, Shakatak is the old-school coast disco in full: two air-conditioned rooms, a garden bar, a monthly 'Dschungel Party' and an annual Miss Southcoast pageant. It shut in the pandemic and fully reopened in August 2022, says its own site, which was last updated in March 2023. If it still runs, nothing happens before midnight, and the late scene is hard-edged and transactional, as coast discos tend to be.
b-shakatak.why: A period piece, if it still runs: have your driver confirm, and plan the way home before you go in.
facts: Central strip, opposite the hotel row
After midnight, Saturday the surest; claims nightly from 21:00 (own site, 2023)
Unverified in 2026: online trail stale since March 2023

b-mangwe.name: The palm-wine dens
b-mangwe.teaser: Mnazi poured hours off the palm, in a village living room you enter introduced or not at all
b-mangwe.story: A mangwe is an unsigned den where mnazi is sold, traditionally by women, and drunk the day it was tapped; the one open door for a visitor is the tasting that ends Kaaribu's Ukunda street-food tour. Without an introduction, don't.
facts: Mnazi from the shared bottle, as the den pours it
The Kaaribu tour, a day ahead: +254 732 905 343
Kaaribu tour USD 25 (seen Aug 2026); the mnazi itself is very cheap

sources.label: Kaaribu: Diani street food and market tour

o-shimba.name: Shimba Hills & Sheldrick Falls
o-shimba.teaser: Kenya's last breeding sable herd on the dawn glades, then a ranger-led walk down to a waterfall
o-shimba.story: Thirty-one kilometres inland the coast turns to forest: 192.5 km² first protected in 1903 and gazetted in 1968, Kenya's largest coastal rainforest and, in KWS's own words, home to the country's last breeding herd of sable antelope. Forest elephants move through it, mist lifts off the glades, and from their edges you look back to the sea. A signed trailhead inside leads down with a ranger to Sheldrick Falls. Come for sable, mist and the falls rather than Mara-style herds: this is forest, not savannah.
o-shimba.why: Be at the gate when it opens: the sable graze the glades early and are gone by the heat.
facts: Via Kombani junction off the Likoni–Ukunda road, 31 km to the gate; gates 06:00–18:00; non-resident USD 50 adult, USD 25 child, cashless (KWS, Oct 2026; old blogs still quote KES 300)
A full day, gate to gate
The ranger-escorted walk to Sheldrick Falls: carry water, wear real shoes
Pack food from Diani: no kitchen inside the reserve has been verified for this guide

o-funzi.name: Funzi & the Ramisi estuary
o-funzi.teaser: Crocodiles on the ebb, a sandbank swim, and crab on the island where the Ramisi meets the sea
o-funzi.story: From Bodo village, about 35 km south of Diani, boats run up the Ramisi River estuary looking for crocodiles where the river meets the ocean. Then comes a swim off a sandbank that exists only at low water, and lunch on Funzi: crab, grilled fish, coconut rice. There is no marine park here; community fees are folded into the operator's price. Crocodiles are not promised, and the sandbank drowns at high water, so timing decides the day. One warning: the Funzi Keys resort is almost certainly not trading, whatever stale listings say.
o-funzi.why: Before you pay, ask the operator for the tide times, and exactly who cooks lunch and where.
facts: Board at Bodo village, about 35 km south; hotel pickup around 07:30. Group trips from about USD 75 (seen Aug 2026); private boats negotiable at Bodo
The sandbank swim, timed to low water
Crab, grilled fish and coconut rice on Funzi

o-mombasa.name: The Biashara Street & Akamba run
o-mombasa.teaser: Mombasa without the ferry: the kanga street in the morning, the carvers' sheds on the airport side
o-mombasa.story: With the Dongo Kundu bypass, Mombasa is a half-day from Diani and the Likoni ferry drops out of the plan: 45 to 75 minutes each way, depending on traffic. The order matters. Start on Biashara Street in the morning, while the kanga houses and their tailors are at work, then swing out to the Akamba carving co-operative in Changamwe, on the airport side, where the sheds are fullest on weekday mornings. Both have their own cards in Crafts & the hand; this card is only the route. If the day stretches, add Mombasa Old Town.
o-mombasa.why: Two stops replace every curio stall on the strip with the real thing.
facts: Via the Dongo Kundu bypass, ferry-free; 45–75 minutes each way
Half a day; a full day with Old Town
The kanga street first, the carving sheds second: both told in Crafts & the hand
Chai on Biashara Street while a tailor hems your kanga

p-mwaepe.name: Mwaepe landing (BMU)
p-mwaepe.teaser: Whole changu, snapper and pweza off the sand at Galu, judged by eye and gill
p-mwaepe.story: Walk down from the Galu hotels on the incoming tide, choose whole reef fish by eye and gill, pay cash and get it on ice at once: ice is what this landing has always lacked, and what the new KSh 256 million landing site, under construction since 2025, is meant to supply. Some kusi mornings nothing comes in; that is the sea.
facts: Whole changu and snapper, pweza; lobster and crab when landed
No; for quantity, ask for the BMU chairman
Negotiated on the sand, cash; no dated prices

sources.label: Citizen Digital: Kwale launches Ksh.256M fish landing site

p-shimoni.name: Shimoni landing & the new port
p-shimoni.teaser: Tuna and kingfish off the channel, landed beside a fish port that is built but not yet working
p-shimoni.story: The channel lands bigger fish than Diani's reef, so buy at the village landing in the morning and loin the tuna on the spot, because the drive home is an hour-plus of warm truck. The KSh 2.6 billion port next door was handed to the Kenya Ports Authority in July 2025 and, at the last dated evidence, still awaited an operator: treat it as in transition, not a market.
facts: Morning; pair it with the dhow day
No; negotiate at the village landing

sources.label: Logistics Business Africa: Shimoni fish port completed

p-names.name: Changu, pweza, tafi: the name ladder
p-names.teaser: A fish's name says where it was caught, with what gear, and what it is worth: learn ten
p-names.story: Fisher Swahili is a technical language, recorded in Heidi Glaesel's coast fieldwork. Changu are the emperors (tangu at Msambweni), tafi the rabbitfish in graded kinds, pono the parrotfish, tewa the groupers, told apart like leopards: tewa chui is the leopard grouper. Kolekole are trevallies, nguru kingfish, jodari tunas, pweza octopus, kamba shrimp, kamba mawe lobster. The ranking is a fallen hierarchy: tafi, changu and pono fill today's catch but were second choice when tuna, marlin and kingfish ran thick, and by the late 1990s kolekole and nguru were already rarely caught. Chambo chema ni baraka ya mvuvi: good bait is the fisher's blessing.
p-names.why: A tewa chui is a trap-and-line lagoon fish; a sulisuli means someone crossed the reef into big water. Treat a cheap nguru with suspicion.
facts: At the Mwaepe, Gazi or Msambweni morning auction: point, ask the name, then ask 'ya leo?' (today's?)
Kitoweo-grade fish by its fisher name: the fish a fisher feeds his own children, never the grade on display

p-market.name: Diani Modern Market, Mvindeni
p-market.teaser: 219 covered stalls with cold storage behind them: where Ukunda's produce trade is moving
p-market.story: Commissioned on 23 May 2026 to replace the open-air Ukunda market, this is where the town's produce trade is moving, and on market days it is already tight. Come for the produce rows; the food court is still settling.
facts: Coconuts in every grade, cassava, greens, citrus; pay cash or M-Pesa

sources.label: The Star: Ruto opens Diani Modern Market (23 May 2026)
Business Today: Diani Modern Market fully operational

p-coconut.name: Madafu, mnazi, mbata, makuti
p-coconut.teaser: Drinking nut, palm wine, copra and thatch: the one tree most coastal farms live off
p-coconut.story: Madafu is the green drinking nut, opened at the roadside with a panga. Mnazi is the tapped palm wine, a morning product drunk the same day; the dens that pour it have their own card in the bars. Mbata is the mature nut, graded for milling into oil or for chewing dry; in the kitchen it is grated on the mbuzi stool and its cream pressed out by hand. Makuti thatch and coir rope use the rest. In Ukunda, Kentaste turns some 30,000 nuts a day from over 4,000 smallholders in Kwale, Kilifi and Mombasa into the cream and virgin oil on Diani's supermarket shelves.
p-coconut.why: Madafu for guests, Kentaste for the pantry, and mnazi only where it is tapped, before noon, never served to guests untested.
facts: Madafu green nut, mnazi palm wine, mbata copra, makuti thatch
Madafu from the beach vendors, KES 50–100 (seen 2026); Kentaste cream and oil at Carrefour and Chandarana
Drink the madafu, hand it back and ask for the kuna: the vendor splits it and cuts a spoon from the shell

p-carrefour.name: Carrefour, Centre Point
p-carrefour.teaser: Fish counter, butchery and bakery at Ukunda junction: for whatever has to stay cold
p-carrefour.story: Kwale County's first Carrefour opened in February 2021, in the Centre Point Plaza anchor space Nakumatt had left empty in 2017: 1,000 m² with a fresh fish counter, butchery, bakery and produce. For a galley it solves what the open market cannot, the cold chain: dairy, dry stores, back-up protein, and Kentaste coconut cream and oil made a few minutes away. Its limits are honest ones. Imported specialty depth, the cheese, charcuterie and wine, runs thinner than in Nairobi, so plan around it or brief the provisioner.
p-carrefour.why: Market at 07:00, the Mwaepe landing by 08:00, Carrefour at 09:00: one loop, one morning.
facts: Dairy, back-up protein, Kentaste coconut cream and oil
Cheese, charcuterie and wine: thinner than Nairobi

sources.label: Business Daily: Carrefour opens new Diani store
Khusoko: Carrefour Kenya opens Diani store

p-chandarana.name: Chandarana Foodplus
p-chandarana.teaser: Masalas, ghee, atta and dry mbaazi mid-strip: the pantry for the coast's own cooking
p-chandarana.story: The Kenyan family-run chain keeps its south-coast branch at Baharini Plaza, and it is the counterweight to Carrefour: specialty, imported and Indian-Kenyan grocery, wines and spirits, with fresh meat and produce beside them. When a recipe wants cardamom, ghee or atta rather than French butter, this is the aisle. It is also where the dry pigeon peas live: buy mbaazi dry and simmer them in coconut for the real coast breakfast. Mid-afternoon is the quiet hour to shop.
p-chandarana.why: The Indian-Kenyan pantry the coast actually cooks with, in one aisle.
facts: Whole spices, ghee, atta, dry mbaazi, pickles, wines and spirits

p-naivas.name: Naivas, The Gate Mall
p-naivas.teaser: Kenya's biggest homegrown chain, inland at Ukunda: water by the crate and staples at local prices
p-naivas.story: The supermarket Ukunda itself uses sits on the Ukunda–Ramisi road at The Gate Mall, a step cheaper than the two beach-road chains. Nothing here is special, and that is the point: dry staples, cleaning supplies, crates of water and soda, the unglamorous volume a galley gets through. Do the bulk here, the cold chain on the strip and the living produce at Mvindeni market, which is on the same road: three stops, three jobs. Published hours conflict, so check before an early run.
p-naivas.why: Bulk at town prices, with the market in the same run.
facts: Dry staples, cleaning, crates of water and soda
Chilled and specialty lines: leave those to the beach-road chains

f-early.name: Kitchens close earlier than you think
f-early.teaser: Some beach kitchens stop at half past eight: after a late dive or a sunset dhow, order by eight
f-early.story: Several beach kitchens on this coast stop serving long before the evening feels over. The Salty Squid is the clearest case, last food orders at 20:30 every night, and it is not alone. If you are coming off a late dive, a sunset dhow or the long drive back from Shimoni, the arithmetic is simple: order by eight, or accept that dinner happens later and elsewhere, at the Ukunda junction grills or at Havana, the one strip kitchen still cooking at midnight.
f-early.why: After nine on the beach road there are two options: eat early, or eat at a junction.
facts: Count on a beach kitchen waiting for a late boat
The Ukunda junction grills or Havana, both in this section

f-midnight.name: Nothing moves before midnight
f-midnight.teaser: The clubs fill after the food has stopped: eat by nine, sand till eleven, then go out
f-midnight.story: The strip's clubs, Shakatak and Manyatta among them, sit empty before midnight and then fill all at once; Shakatak's own site says as much. So the sequence that works is the reverse of what visitors try: eat properly by nine, drink on the sand until eleven, go out after that. Do it the other way round and you end up hungry after the kitchens have shut. Both clubs are flagged unverified: their 2024 press trail from the streetlight-led revival went cold, so confirm on the day.
f-midnight.why: Confirm any club the same day: a cold paper trail is the warning, not a footnote.
facts: Eat by 21:00, the sand until 23:00, then out
Any club, the same day, through your driver

f-junction.name: The Ukunda junction, just after sunset
f-junction.teaser: Where the boda riders eat after dark: viazi karai and mishkaki, still going when the beach road is quiet
f-junction.story: The late plate that depends on no single kitchen: at the town's transport crossroads the charcoal and karai pans keep going after the beach road has gone quiet, because the people who run the strip eat here on the way home. Pick the stall with a queue of boda riders and fresh frying in view.
facts: Viazi karai with chilli-tamarind, mishkaki, grilled corn
From about 16:00 until late; best just after sunset
No: walk up, point, pay cash or M-Pesa
KES 20 corn to low hundreds (seen May 2026)

f-havana.name: Havana's late kitchen
f-havana.teaser: The strip kitchen still feeding people at one in the morning, every night of the week
f-havana.story: When the beach kitchens have stopped, Havana is still grilling calamari: the answer if you are on the strip and would rather not take a taxi to the junction. Late service is the first thing to go in low season, so check the night before you rely on it.

f-funky.name: Funky Monkey, to midnight
f-funky.teaser: The bar that bridges the dead hours between the kitchens closing and the clubs waking, Wed–Sat
f-funky.story: The kitchen stops at 21:30, so eat early, but the bar runs to midnight Wednesday to Saturday and carries the hours before the clubs wake. Wednesday is Hot Salsa night: DJs, dancers, margarita flights.
facts: Food before 21:30, then a margarita flight
Wednesday for the salsa; Wed–Sat to midnight
WhatsApp a table for salsa night: +254 742 794 527

Ibiza Market not named. b-funky and f-funky both point to funky-monkey with separate angles (the drink and awards vs. the late hours and Wednesday salsa). Cut clubs Full Moon and Tandoori appear only in b-manyatta as 'also listed in 2024, nothing verifiable'; f-midnight names only Shakatak and Manyatta.
